Protocol note: default headless silently falls back to SwiftShader-Vulkan; real-GPU checks must force --use-angle=d3d11 (permanent utility tools/gpu-check.mjs added). Root cause: wet-band roughness 0.34 + mip-averaged detail normals = GGX speckle clusters on banks/pan rims. Fix (terrain material.js/water.js): wet roughness 0.50, +0.35 roughness floor over 200-800 m, detail normals flatten to 15% past 700 m, water glint x0.1 by 800 m, odd-angle tile rotations. Grass mottle + dirt cracks (textures.js): the streak stamp is now a locally-rotated domain-warped two-octave field with a patchy mask; cracks are a wobbled two-scale worley at half contrast; palette colours untouched. FOURTH AND DEEPEST ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-05: environment/atmosphere.js lightDepth() reused scatter()'s view-density scratch array _d, so every CPU-sampled sky radiance came out ~10^4x too dim (measured zenith 7e-6 vs physical ~0.5). The exposure controller, reading a near-black sky, climbed to its ceiling; the visible 'sky' was the blown-out cloud deck; fog and aerial-perspective colours near black produced the horizon band. This is the true root cause of the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'washed out toward white' blocker and of both of environment's round-2 majors — NOT ACES tone mapping, NOT albedo authoring. The GPU LUT was unaffected (GLSL locals), which is why sun colour was always right while sky/fog colours were wrong. Fixed with a separate scratch array; wave-3 verification then proceeded against a correctly-lit world.

Wave 3 (savannah, park) verified 2026-09-05: both modules were already fully implemented in the ZIP but had never been screenshotted, scored, or documented (STATUS said 'not-started' — stale). All 17 savannah presets and 7 park presets + 9 full-game sweeps shot and READ; 0 console errors everywhere; all inside the draw/triangle budgets. savannah README written; park README's two placeholder sections filled with measured numbers; missing READMEs written for environment, simulation, ui, audio; traffic's 1-line draft replaced.

Screenshot-tooling note for future rounds: park's own setSpeed(1) used to push every capture into a random night hour under SwiftShader (~35 game-hours burn during the 40-frame settle at ~1 fps) — capture pages must pass &speed=0, and modules that advance the clock must respect an explicitly paused clock. Also: do not run 3+ concurrent SwiftShader renders on a 12-core machine — module imports starve and pages time out.
Egress proxy blocks Poly Haven / ambientCG / all CDNs: every asset is procedural.
Screenshot tool renders through SwiftShader (software GL); fps in shots/*.json is NOT a GPU number. Draw calls, triangles and errors are real.

Wave 1 was interrupted mid-round by an API spend limit. Builders were killed before writing module READMEs and before their final iteration passes. Scores below are the ORCHESTRATOR's own integration review, not a full critic pass: fewer angles, no API-contract audit. Treat them as provisional and biased slightly optimistic on modules only seen at one preset.
Integration verified: all 15 modules load together in the full game with zero console errors, 278 draw calls, 4.74 M triangles (park's demo auto-builds on core:ready).

SECOND ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: environment/index.js clamped auto-exposure at 60x, and it was hitting 5.46x at golden hour / 60x at night on ordinary, correctly-lit scenes (Math.max(0, keyDir.y) kills the key-light term well before the sky actually looks dim as the sun nears the horizon). Every material several-fold overexposed, verified by reading a baked lion albedo texture directly (correct ~0.38 linear) against near-white on screen. Lowered the ceiling to 4 (commit e3a6999); night is now dim and legible with visible stars instead of blown to white, golden hour shows correct value separation between light/dark test objects instead of clipping everything. Needs a further tuning pass against real references but is no longer broken. This, independently of the sRGB double-encode, explains why several modules' screenshots looked washed out at low sun angles even after the sRGB fix — e.g. buildings' lodge preset (tod 17.5) flat-white background buildings.

THIRD ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-04: terrain/mesh.js had `mesh.receiveShadow = false; // BENCH`, a leftover benchmarking flag that silently blocked every shadow in the game from landing on the ground, anywhere. Fixed (commit e3a6999). This was the real cause of animals' round-1 'no contact shadow' blocker — animals had already shipped a drawn contact-shadow decal as a workaround, which stays in place as a complement now that real shadows also work.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-02: core/Textures.js gpu() double-encoded sRGB (shader-side linearToSRGBv plus an sRGB-internal-format render target). Linear 0.216 was stored as byte 188 instead of 128 — every albedo ~37% too bright. This, not ACES tone mapping, was the real cause of the project-wide washed-out look; the earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a core defect and is now WRONG. Core is fixed. Modules that compensated must have that compensation REMOVED: props is currently over-dark (near-black foliage), and any darkening added to animals/terrain/roads in round 2 must be re-checked.

issues.text: Toolbar active-tool pill renders a literal "null" as visible text (confirmed via innerHTML dump: "Building.Placenull...."). Root cause: pill.append(...) uses the native Element.append(), which stringifies a null child, instead of the project's own append() helper in dom.js which skips null/undefined. Fires in the module's own toolbar showcase preset.

Side panel can show "0% HAPPY / Miserable" contradicted by healthy need bars (83/50/52/65/77%) and "Doing fine" advice text. Root cause: animals.getHappiness(id) returns a hard 0 fallback for any id unknown to the real animals module registry -- exactly what happens for mock/showcase-injected animals (ui/mock.js writes directly into world.animals, bypassing animals.spawn()). The selected animal is also entirely absent from the 3D view for the same reason. Fires in the module's own panel showcase preset.

update()'s 0.5s refresh accumulator is wall-clock based, not frame-count based -- plausibly fires every frame under SwiftShader's slow frame time instead of twice a second, inflating measured updateMs (7.4-9.7ms EMA vs the 1.5ms/module budget); likely a measurement artifact of software GL rather than a confirmed real-hardware violation, but worth a frame-time-independent cap.
Empty notification panel container can appear; population/cash graph panel is a stub vs spec -- both already disclosed in the README.

issues.text: FIXED and verified (tools/shots/sav-kopje-fix-d.png / -e.png, 2026-09-07; RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 with a fresh 1080p capture, blind4-sav-kopje.png): the male lion is unmistakable at 8 m — dark mane, tan flank, legs grounded, a lioness standing right third and another lying left, kopje backdrop, sun behind the lens. Root cause was three stacked occluders invisible to the terrain-only LOS check: the spot sat on the kopje's steep skirt (legs swallowed by a rock lip), a tall dead shrub ~3 m off the cleared lane leaned across the subject, and a giant boulder rooted beside the lens filled half the frame; dead-centre front light also flattened the male toward the old 'pale box'. showcase.js now requires dry AND slope < 0.14 at the spot, seeds the bearing 20° off the sun for three-quarter light, marches the camera (8→30 m) requiring camera-spot slope < 0.18, and widens props.clear to a ±3.5 m corridor, a 9 m podium at the male, a 5 m patch per lioness and a 20 m fore-court at the lens; hold pins behaviour so the settle cannot wander the pride off. Both captures use an identical camera (d=8, pitch 10, yaw −87.1°) — the lottery is gone. Draw calls 185 (was 190); waterhole unchanged at 200. Remaining nit: the male's flank reads pale-bright at full front-rake — a lighting tune, not an occlusion defect.

FIXED and verified (2026-09-21, same day it was filed): the pan-centre black patch under the acacia canopy. Root cause in terrain/water.js's custom lighting: the water's analytic sky-reflection term collapses toward its 0.015 Fresnel floor at near-top-down viewing angles (physically correct), and with the real-time shadow zeroing direct diffuse and envMapIntensity deliberately kept low (0.10, to stop the river reading as a sheet of white sky — see the module's own history), a fully-shadowed patch had no light left to render with. Pixel readback confirmed it: byte ~12/channel, well below even the water's own 'near-black olive at depth' body-colour asymptote (linear 0.03 alone renders ~byte 48). Fixed with a small unconditional in-column-scatter floor (`outgoingLight += diffuseColor.rgb * 0.45`) — negligible on lit water (roads-bridge-waterfix-check.png shows the river's dark tannin colour and depth absorption unchanged), the only light source in full shade. After: the patch reads as plausible dappled shade (~55/43/25 vs ~80/65/40 in full sun, a believable falloff) instead of a hard black hole (sav-waterhole-blackfix2.png).

issues.text: DONE (2026-09-21): round-4 blind visual test re-ran the exact round-3 protocol at 1920x1080 (game.blindVisual 6.9 -> 7.8; savannah subset 7.0 -> 7.9). Confirmed resolved: waterline sparkle (the most-cited round-3 defect, gone from both game and savannah overview shots), kopje pride legibility, grass mottle stamp, tiled crack motif. New/carried-over finding filed under savannah: a hard black patch in the waterhole's pan centre. Full per-image scores and a discrepancy note (game-close-21.5 did not read as legible as environment's own 09-08 history note claims — see below) in docs/critic/game-round4-blind.md.

Discrepancy found 2026-09-21, then explained (not code-fixed): environment's STATUS history claims the live game's `close` camera preset at 21.5h (game-close-21_5-tune2.png, 09-08) reads '~7, terrain mottle and lodge roof all read'. A fresh capture of the same core camera preset (CameraRig.js: target [0,0], distance 140, pitch 28, yaw 55) at the same hour this round reads close to the original 5.5 instead. Traced it with an in-page ray march (camera.matrixWorld's forward axis, sampled against props' own coverAt(x,z) API every 10 m) rather than guessing: the camera's own position sits at (101, 69, 71) with 73% ground-projected tree cover directly under/around it. At pitch 28° / distance 140, this preset sits ~66 m up — despite being labelled 'ground detail' in CameraRig.js, it's a moderately elevated 3/4 angle, not an eye-level shot — so nearby tree crowns seen from above/beside at that elevation legitimately dominate the near-field. At night, self-shadowed canopy tops read dark even with the moon-key lift and hemisphere floor active (both correctly lift the open ground/midground, visible past the canopy in this same shot) — this is the same 'foreground self-shadowed canopies stay near-black by design' limitation environment's own README already documents, just unusually prominent here because this fixed camera happens to sit inside a dense tree cluster. Most likely explanation for the 09-08 claim: that verification shot was taken before a later terrain/props density change added more canopy near world origin, or from a state where this exact spot had less cover. Not a regression in the night-ambient fix itself and not worth chasing further as a shader fix (would require rethinking canopy self-shadowing generally, disproportionate to a fixed-camera corner case); a camera restage of this one preset was considered and rejected because it's shared with the well-regarded close-14 daytime shot.

FIXED (2026-09-05, environment/atmosphere.js): the round-1 SYSTEMIC 'everything washes out toward white' blocker was never a tone-mapping or albedo-authoring problem — it was a CPU sky-sampler aliasing bug that made every sky-derived colour ~10^4x too dim, driving the exposure controller to its ceiling and fog/horizon colours to near-black. Full root cause under environment's entry. The earlier 'author darker to compensate' guidance was a workaround over a defect and is wrong.
